correctness.rationale: For each n>=2, all de Bruijn edges are distinct n-bit windows of weights 1 or 2; degree counting and unique root-edge normalization are exact. Every weight-two state has a forced zero exit until a weight-one state; the reduced one-weight transitions are i->i+1 (top -> root) or i->m-1-i. If an upper index chooses one, its interval [m-1-i,i] is closed, and the root is unreachable. Lower indices allow either edge and strictly increase index; these choices give all in-arborescences, exactly 2^floor(m/2). The balanced graph is therefore Eulerian and BEST has factorial factor one, giving the stated count. Independent exact direct DFS and matrix-tree computations agree for n=2..11; the proof handles arbitrary n.

value.rationale: Classifies and counts every realization of a natural two-layer binary de Bruijn universal cycle for all lengths; completes a natural enumeration problem downstream of active work on weighted cut-down sequences.
